synopsis: Occlusion and sensor obstruction are central validation risks: perception in dust, rain, mud and occlusion is identified as the hardest technical gap, and brakes cannot recover safety margin when reliable detection range falls below required stopping distance [f10338, f6585]. Virtual testing is useful for camera and lidar geometry and occlusion, but simplified sensor models require explicit encoding of partial occlusion, while lens and cover soiling and its accumulation, drying and cleaning remain poorly reproduced [f1736, f1740, f4479, f4772]. Acceptance requirements address both hidden targets and blocked sensors: MOSH Rev 1 requires detection without line-of-sight, while on-road FMVSS 127 requires detection and communication of obstruction-related degradation; the program still needs explicit blockage, maintenance and calibration requirements [f2458, f2000, f2929, f7463]. Variant validation may need several physical representatives because worst stopping distance and worst occlusion need not coincide, and mounting changes and non-monotonic geometry effects undermine unproven transfer across a fleet of 100+ models [f626, f7919, f7921, f10589]. Physical correlation and trustworthy reference labels remain essential: high-value occlusion phenomena need physical reference tests, ground truth needs an unavailable-or-ambiguous state, and published reference-stack validation across the full mining-condition set was not found [f7374, f5394, f5399].
